title: PT leader in the Chamber falls ill and sessions are suspended
seoTitle: PT leader falls ill, vote halted
subtitle: Pedro Uczai received medical care after fainting at the Leaders' College meeting
excerpt: During the Leaders' College meeting, PT leader in the Chamber, Pedro Uczai, fell ill, was rescued, and the vote was halted.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Tuesday morning (the 11th), Pedro Uczai, PT leader in the Chamber of Deputies, felt unwell during the Leaders' College meeting. The episode culminated in a fainting spell, requiring immediate intervention from fellow parliamentarians.

Emergency care

Among the parliamentarians who provided assistance was Hugo Motta, the House president and a trained physician. He, together with other deputies, escorted Uczai to the Chamber's Medical Department, where the health team took over care. The parliamentarian remained under observation until his vital signs were stabilized.

Reaction from PT leadership

In an official statement, PT leadership reported that the leader felt unwell, fainted, but regained consciousness and was stabilized. The communication emphasized that the parliamentarian received the necessary support and that his condition was monitored by the House's professionals.

Impact on legislative activities

Following the incident, the voting session was suspended until the situation could be assessed. The interruption demonstrates the priority given to the safety and well‑being of Chamber members, in line with internal procedures that mandate suspension of work in cases of medical emergencies.

Institutional context

  • Leaders' College: internal body that brings together party and bloc representatives to coordinate the legislative agenda.
  • Chamber Medical Department: unit responsible for providing immediate assistance to parliamentarians and staff in urgent situations.
  • Party leader: deputy who represents and organizes his party's actions within the Chamber, influencing debates and votes.

The incident highlights the importance of health protocols in public institutions and the need for a rapid response when a member shows signs of physical compromise.

With information from Agência Brasil.
